risks.title: Single database with no replica or backup configuration
risks.why: The model has one database and none of the files read mention a replica, a standby, a backup tool or a managed database service.
risks.check: Confirm where backups are taken and that a restore has been tried. Decide whether a replica or a managed service is worth its cost for this project.

fixes.text: Take scheduled backups and rehearse a restore.
fixes.tradeoff: Costs storage and an hour of practice; it protects against loss, not against downtime.

fixes.text: Use a managed database that handles backups and failover.
fixes.tradeoff: Less control and a monthly bill; fewer things to run yourself.

fixes.text: Add a read replica or standby.
fixes.tradeoff: Costs money and adds replication lag; a replica is not a backup.

risks.title: Secret-looking variable exposed to the browser
risks.why: A variable with a browser-exposed prefix (NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_ and similar) has a name containing SECRET, PRIVATE, KEY, TOKEN or PASSWORD. Such variables are copied into the public JavaScript bundle. Only the name was read, never the value.
risks.check: Check whether the value is really meant to be public. If it is a secret, move it to the server and rotate it, because it may already be in a deployed bundle.

fixes.text: Move the value to the server and call it from there.
fixes.tradeoff: One more request hop for the browser.

fixes.text: If it was a secret, rotate it, because it may already be in a deployed bundle.
fixes.tradeoff: Anything using the old value must be updated.
